title: General Insurance Corporation of India - 540755 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: GIC Re H1 FY27 PAT fell to INR4,377.66 crore (from INR4,619.02 crore) as underwriting loss widened to INR1,709.06 crore; combined ratio 107.39%.
summary.overview: Gross premium grew to INR24,703.57 crore in H1 FY27 from INR21,989.71 crore, with domestic premium up 15.9% and international flat. Q2 combined ratio rose to 110.23% from 109.15%, with incurred claims ratio at 87.39% versus 81.50%, while H1 combined ratio was broadly flat at 107.39%. Q2 profit before tax and profit after tax both declined YoY, helped by NSE-related investment income of INR1,082 crore. Management provided about INR450-500 crore for Gujarat floods, flagged possible lagged cat losses in Q3, and declined to give NATCAT quantification or an FY27 combined ratio target.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 domestic premium INR19,794.41 crore (80% of total), up 15.9% YoY; domestic H1 loss ratio about 88% per analyst, with growth driven by health quota shares and standalone health insurer signings, while property book shrank.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 international premium INR4,909.16 crore (20%), broadly flat YoY; combined ratio improved to 108.24% from 119.87% but still not underwriting profitable. Q1 loss ratio was 66% and H1 was about 80%, with Motor and Cargo reserve strengthening on a 2021 run-off treaty.

segments.name: Health and Life Re
segments.commentary: Health and Life grew strongly on big-ticket contracts written from 1 April; health faces pricing pressure and underwriting losses, and Life Re reserve strengthening over recent quarters is said to be complete, with Q2 Life Re results improving QoQ.

guidance_outlook: No NATCAT loss quantification or guidance for Q1/Q2; explicit guidance proposed from FY28.
Management believes a 105% full-year combined ratio is achievable but cites two remaining quarters and Q3 cat exposure.

Ind AS transition: management will not comment on combined ratio; expects deflation to the extent of mark-to-market, with reserve discounting the major driver and possible large first-year investment gains.
Gujarat flood provision of about INR450-500 crore booked in Q2; further lagged cat losses possible in subsequent quarters.
Eastern India cyclone losses: management estimates GIC Re loss at 25-30% of reported industry loss, data not yet received.
Competitive pressure in international market expected to persist for another year; January and April 2027 renewal pricing to be the key test.
capex_capacity: Foreign portfolio held near INR4,900 crore per half-year; management is pursuing broker outreach ahead of 1 January renewals to grow the book.
Reserve strengthening: IBNR reportedly rose to about INR5,100 crore from about INR4,000 crore a year earlier (per analyst), including crop-year strengthening for drought conditions.
Advances on the balance sheet reportedly up about 10% standalone and 28% consolidated since March; management said it is normal and will revert with details.
demand_pricing: Management says domestic property rates have held since September 2026 after a slide in premiums, per market information.
Global reinsurance capacity is abundant, including alternative capital and new reinsurers; competition expected to persist.
Management is prioritising pricing adequacy and risk-adjusted returns over premium growth.
Health pricing is under pressure; GIC Re is focusing on retail rather than group health.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify Q2 NATCAT/flood losses versus modelled run rate; is a 105% FY27 combined ratio achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will not disclose NATCAT guidance until FY28; it believes 105% is achievable but two quarters remain, including cat-exposed Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the domestic loss ratio improve despite industry Gujarat flood losses, and is cat provision adequate?
qa_highlights.answer: There is a reporting lag, so some losses may appear next quarter; INR450-500 crore has been provided for Gujarat floods, with results between full market loss and zero.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the international loss ratio rise from 66% in Q1 to 80% in H1, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Property performed well, offset by provisions on Motor and Cargo for a 2021 US run-off treaty, which management called conservative accounting; overall foreign book deteriorated slightly.

qa_highlights.question: Growth drivers in domestic business and whether market share is gained from FRBs or GIFT City units; health line detail?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is from big-ticket health quota shares and standalone health insurer signings, with property shrinking; the 4% obligatory cessions reflect market growth.

qa_highlights.question: NSE contribution to PBT and accounting treatment?
qa_highlights.answer: NSE contributed INR1,082 crore from the OFS; the stake was at cost while unlisted and is now at market value, with unrealised gains going to the fair value change account, not investment income.

qa_highlights.question: Will IBNR strengthening continue in H2, and why did advances rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Actuary said IBNR follows business written and is not a policy choice; management cited crop-year drought strengthening and reserve releases on other contracts. Advances rise was described as normal, with details to follow.

qa_highlights.question: Cyclone losses in eastern India and competitive threat from new reinsurers?
qa_highlights.answer: No concrete cyclone figure yet; GIC Re may bear 25-30% of the industry loss. Management will watch new reinsurers' behaviour before judging competition.

risks_watch: Q3 FY27 catastrophe losses and lagged Gujarat flood and eastern cyclone losses could push Q3 combined ratio higher.
International combined ratio of 108.24% remains above 100% and the foreign book is flat; January 2027 renewal outcome is key.
Reserve strengthening in health, Life Re, and crop lines versus releases; net reserve movements are hard to read.
Ind AS transition from FY28 may change reported combined ratio and ROE; the first year may show large investment gains.
Domestic property rate discipline since September 2026 must hold; new reinsurer entrants may add pressure.
Balance sheet advances growth (about 28% consolidated) is unexplained so far.
summary.management_tone: Cautious and somewhat evasive on forward numbers: management declined to quantify NATCAT losses, Ind AS combined ratio, and reserve drivers, deferring to the January renewal and later disclosures. Tone was confident on solvency (4.18) and the international combined-ratio improvement, but it acknowledged underwriting losses and reserve strengthening.
key_quotes: Presently, we are not disclosing this. We are working on it, and we propose to come up with this guidance explicitly from the next year.
Strengthening underwriting profitability remains a key priority, and our efforts are directed towards better risk selection, appropriate pricing, and active portfolio management.
It is conservative accounting. As the IBNR proportion is small, it is better to maintain it at certain threshold levels.

growth.why: No explicit revenue growth guidance; Q2 gross premium rose 16.9% YoY (H1 +12.3%) driven by domestic health quota shares and standalone health signings, but management is prioritising pricing adequacy over premium growth, cites persistent international competition, and the only margin guide (105% FY27 combined ratio) is hedged as "believed, not committed" with no capacity or order book backing.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management believes a 105% FY27 combined ratio is achievable versus H1 at 107.39% and Q2 at 110.23%, but it is hedged and Q3 cat exposure plus lagged Gujarat flood and eastern cyclone losses (GIC Re may bear 25-30% of industry loss) cut against it.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capacity or new plant/branch build-out was not discussed; growth is from quota shares and health signings, not new capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Gross premium rose 16.9% in Q2 and 12.3% in H1 to INR24,703.57 crore, with domestic premium up 15.9% from health quota shares and standalone health signings, though management is prioritising pricing over premium growth and international is flat at about INR4,900 crore per half.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex announcement or utilisation metric discussed; this is an insurer, so the capex trigger does not apply directly.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to quantify NATCAT losses or give an FY27 combined ratio target and only said it would like to believe 105% is achievable, with H1 at 107.39% and Q2 at 110.23%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 is cat-exposed with lagged Gujarat flood (INR450-500 crore provided) and eastern cyclone losses still unquantified, and the International combined ratio of 108.24% stays above 100%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launch was discussed.

rows.label: International renewal pricing test (Jan and Apr 2027)
rows.why: Competition in international reinsurance is expected to persist another year and the January 2027 and April 2027 renewals are the key test, with the international combined ratio at 108.24%.

rows.label: Life Re reserve strengthening complete
rows.why: Management says Life Re reserve strengthening is complete and Q2 Life Re results improved QoQ, though health pricing pressure and underwriting losses persist.

rows.label: Ind AS transition from FY28
rows.why: Management expects deflation to the extent of mark-to-market and possible large first-year investment gains, but will not comment on the combined ratio under Ind AS.
